title: NCL Mine Surveyor Mock 16
pattern: 100 MCQs, 100 marks, 90 min, NO negative marking

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'reverse fault' is characterised by:
options: Hanging wall moves up relative to the footwall (compression)
questions.solution: Reverse fault: hanging wall is thrust up relative to footwall (compressional regime).

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'strike-slip fault' involves:
questions.solution: Strike-slip faults have predominantly horizontal displacement.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: An 'anticlinal axis' on a geological map is the line connecting:
options: The highest points (hinges) of the oldest beds on each limb
The lowest points of the fold
questions.solution: The anticlinal axis traces the hinge line of the anticline.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'synclinal axis' connects the:
questions.solution: The synclinal axis traces the hinge line where the youngest beds are preserved.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: To determine the 'true thickness' of a bed from its outcrop width, one needs:
options: Both the first and second options
Neither the first nor the second option
Outcrop width, dip of the bed, and angle of the section line to strike
questions.solution: True thickness = outcrop width × sin(dip) × cos(α), where α is the angle between the section and the dip direction.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'outcrop width' of a bed is influenced by:
options: This is not applicable in this context
Both the first and second options
Neither the first nor the second option
Bed thickness, dip angle, and topographic slope
questions.solution: Outcrop width depends on true thickness, dip, and the relationship between dip and topographic slope.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'borehole correlation' on a geological map involves:
options: Matching rock units between boreholes to establish lateral continuity
questions.solution: Correlation links rock units identified in different boreholes based on lithology and fossils.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'formation thickness' from borehole data is calculated using:
options: Depth to top and depth to bottom of the formation
questions.solution: Formation thickness = depth to bottom - depth to top (corrected for dip if inclined).

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'cross-section' from a geological map is constructed by:
options: Projecting surface geology onto a vertical plane along a section line
questions.solution: A cross-section projects geological features from the map onto a vertical plane.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'horizontal displacement' of a fault is the:
options: Net slip measured along the strike direction
questions.solution: Heave = horizontal displacement; throw = vertical displacement of a fault.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'vertical separation' (throw) of a fault is the:
options: Vertical displacement of beds across the fault
questions.solution: Throw is the vertical component of fault displacement.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'dyke' on a geological map is shown as:
options: A narrow, roughly linear body cutting across existing rocks
questions.solution: Dykes are tabular intrusive bodies that cut across pre-existing rock layers.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'sill' differs from a 'dyke' in that a sill is:
options: Parallel to the bedding of the host rock
questions.solution: Sills are concordant (parallel to bedding); dykes are discordant (cutting across bedding).

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'dip direction' is perpendicular to the:
questions.solution: Dip direction is always at 90° to the strike direction, pointing in the direction of maximum slope.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: On a geological map, 'contour lines' that V upstream across a valley indicate the beds:
questions.solution: If contours of a bed V upstream, the bed dips in the same direction as the valley flows (downstream to upstream = upstream V = bed dips upstream).

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'horizontal bed' on a geological map shows outcrop patterns that:
options: Follow the topographic contour lines exactly
questions.solution: Horizontal beds outcrop along topographic contours.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'vertical bed' on a geological map has an outcrop pattern that:
options: Is a straight line regardless of topography
questions.solution: Vertical beds outcrop as straight lines on the map, unaffected by topography.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'law of superposition' states that in an undisturbed sequence, the oldest bed is:
questions.solution: In an undisturbed sequence, the oldest beds are at the bottom and youngest at the top.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'principle of original horizontality' states that sedimentary beds are originally deposited in approximately:
questions.solution: Sediments are deposited nearly horizontally; tilting/folding occurred after deposition.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'facies change' on a geological map indicates:
options: A lateral change in rock character within the same formation
questions.solution: Facies change = lateral variation in lithology (e.g., sandstone grading to shale).

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'marker horizon' in coal geology is:
options: A distinctive, laterally persistent bed used for correlation
questions.solution: Marker horizons (e.g., a distinctive shale, limestone, or volcanic ash bed) are used to correlate strata.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'cleat' in coal refers to:
options: The natural fracture system in coal, typically perpendicular to bedding
questions.solution: Cleats are systematic fractures in coal, usually in two sets perpendicular to each other and to bedding.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'rank' of coal indicates its:
options: Degree of metamorphism (from peat to anthracite)
questions.solution: Coal rank increases from peat → lignite → sub-bituminous → bituminous → anthracite.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'coal plume' or 'dirt band' within a seam is significant because:
options: It affects mining and coal preparation (must be removed)
questions.solution: Dirt bands (partings) reduce coal quality and must be separated during processing.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'calorific value' of coal is measured in:
options: Kilocalories per kilogram or BTU per pound
questions.solution: Calorific value (CV) indicates the heat energy released per unit mass of coal.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'borehole log' records:
options: Neither the first nor the second option
This applies to a different field entirely
The lithology, formations, coal seams, and water strikes encountered
questions.solution: A borehole log is a continuous record of formations encountered during drilling.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'water strike' in a borehole is:
options: The depth at which water was first encountered during drilling
questions.solution: Water strike = depth at which groundwater was first struck during drilling.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'coal ash content' refers to:
options: The inorganic residue remaining after complete combustion
questions.solution: Ash is the non-combustible mineral matter remaining after coal is burned.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'volatile matter' in coal consists of:
options: Gases and tars released when coal is heated in the absence of air
questions.solution: Volatile matter includes hydrocarbons, CO, H₂, and other gases driven off during devolatilisation.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'cross-section' drawn perpendicular to the strike shows the true dip of beds, while a section at an angle shows:
options: An apparent dip (less than true dip)
questions.solution: Apparent dip < true dip; the section must be parallel to the dip direction to show true dip.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The relationship between true dip (δ) and apparent dip (α) at angle θ to strike is:
questions.solution: Apparent dip formula: tan(α) = tan(δ) × sin(θ), where θ is the angle between the section and the strike.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: On a geological map, the 'boundary' between two formations is a:
options: Line (contact line) showing where the two rock units meet at the surface
questions.solution: Formation boundaries are mapped as lines showing where the contact between units outcrops.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: An 'inlier' on a geological map is an area of:
options: Older rocks surrounded by younger rocks
Younger rocks surrounded by older rocks
questions.solution: An inlier = older rocks surrounded by younger (the inverse of an outlier).

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: An 'outlier' on a geological map is an area of:
options: Older rocks surrounded by younger rocks
Younger rocks isolated within older rocks
questions.solution: An outlier = younger rocks surrounded by older (e.g., a remnant of an overlying formation).

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'cleavage' in folded rocks is:
options: A secondary fabric formed parallel to the axial plane of folds
questions.solution: Cleavage develops parallel to the axial plane during folding.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: An 'isogon' on a geological map connects points of:
questions.solution: Isogons (dip isogons) connect points of equal dip on a folded surface.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: Surpac is a software package primarily used for:
options: Mine planning, geological modelling, and surveying
questions.solution: Surpac is a leading 3D mine planning and geological modelling software.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: AutoCAD is classified as a:
questions.solution: AutoCAD is a widely used CAD software for 2D drafting and 3D modelling.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'point cloud' in LiDAR processing refers to:
options: A large set of 3D data points representing a surface or object
questions.solution: LiDAR point clouds contain millions of x, y, z points representing the scanned surface.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: RTK GPS provides positioning accuracy of approximately:
questions.solution: Real-Time Kinematic GPS achieves centimetre-level accuracy (1-2 cm horizontal).

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'base station' in RTK GPS survey is:
options: A stationary receiver at a known coordinate that provides corrections
questions.solution: The base station at a known point broadcasts corrections to the rover for real-time positioning.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: GIS stands for:
questions.solution: GIS = Geographic Information System for capturing, storing, and analysing spatial data.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: In GIS, a 'vector' data model represents features as:
questions.solution: Vector data uses points, lines (arcs), and polygons to represent features.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: In GIS, a 'raster' data model represents features as:
questions.solution: Raster data divides the area into a grid of cells, each with a value.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'digital terrain model' (DTM) in Surpac is used for:
questions.solution: Surpac DTM creates triangulated irregular networks (TIN) to model surfaces.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'coordinate geometry' (COGO) functions in survey software are used for:
options: Computing coordinates, distances, and angles from survey measurements
questions.solution: COGO computes positions from traverse data, intersection, resection, and other survey methods.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'total station' combines which instruments?
options: Electronic theodolite and Electronic Distance Measurement (EDM)
questions.solution: A total station integrates an electronic theodolite (angle measurement) with EDM (distance measurement).

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'GNSS' system includes:
options: Neither the first nor the second option
Both the first and second options
questions.solution: GNSS = Global Navigation Satellite System, encompassing all satellite navigation systems.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'drone' (UAV) survey in mining is used for:
options: Topographic mapping, stockpile volume calculation, and progress monitoring
questions.solution: Drones provide rapid topographic data, volume calculations, and visual monitoring.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: Structure from Motion (SfM) photogrammetry requires:
options: Multiple overlapping photographs from different positions
This is valid only under special circumstances
questions.solution: SfM needs overlapping images taken from different viewpoints to reconstruct 3D geometry.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'LiDAR equation' relates the received power to:
options: Neither the first nor the second option
This applies to a different field entirely
Target reflectivity, range, atmospheric conditions, and system parameters
questions.solution: LiDAR equation: P_r ∝ (P_t × ρ × A_r) / (R² × Ω), considering all system and target parameters.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'ground-penetrating radar' (GPR) in mining is used to:
options: Detect subsurface features, voids, and geological boundaries
questions.solution: GPR sends electromagnetic pulses into the ground and maps reflections from subsurface interfaces.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'point density' of a LiDAR survey is measured in:
questions.solution: Point density = number of laser returns per unit area (pts/m²).

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: In AutoCAD, the 'LINE' command creates:
options: A straight line segment between two points
questions.solution: The LINE command draws straight segments defined by start and end points.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'POLYLINE' command in AutoCAD creates:
options: A connected sequence of line and/or arc segments as a single object
questions.solution: A polyline is a single object made of connected line and arc segments.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'TRIM' command in AutoCAD is used to:
options: Cut objects at a cutting edge boundary
questions.solution: TRIM removes portions of objects up to a defined cutting edge.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'OFFSET' command in AutoCAD creates:
options: A parallel copy of an object at a specified distance
questions.solution: OFFSET creates a concentric or parallel copy at a specified distance.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: In Surpac, a 'string' represents:
options: A line or boundary defined by a sequence of 3D points
questions.solution: In Surpac, strings define features (faults, boundaries, contours) as point sequences.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'DTM' (Digital Terrain Model) in Surpac is created using:
options: Neither the first nor the second option
questions.solution: Surpac creates a TIN (Triangulated Irregular Network) DTM from surveyed points.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'block model' in Surpac is used for:
options: Resource estimation by dividing the orebody into 3D blocks
questions.solution: Block models subdivide the orebody into regular 3D cells, each assigned grade/value.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'kriging' method in resource estimation is a:
options: Geostatistical interpolation method that provides best linear unbiased estimates
questions.solution: Kriging uses spatial statistics (semivariogram) to interpolate values with minimum estimation variance.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'semivariogram' in geostatistics describes:
options: The spatial continuity/variability of a regionalised variable
questions.solution: A semivariogram plots semivariance vs. distance to characterise spatial correlation.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: In GIS, 'overlay analysis' involves:
options: Combining two or more thematic layers to create a new layer
questions.solution: Overlay combines layers (e.g., geology + soil + slope) for multi-criteria analysis.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'buffer' in GIS is created by:
options: Generating a zone of specified distance around a feature
questions.solution: Buffer analysis creates zones (e.g., 500m around a river) for proximity studies.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'volume calculation' from a DTM in mining software uses:
options: Triangulated surfaces above and below, computing the difference
Neither the first nor the second option
This is valid only under special circumstances
questions.solution: Volumes are calculated by comparing two triangulated surfaces (e.g., original vs. current terrain).

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: An 'orthophoto' generated from drone imagery is:
options: A geometrically corrected photo with uniform scale, usable as a map
questions.solution: Orthophotos are corrected for terrain displacement and can be used for planimetric measurement.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'flight planning' for a drone survey considers:
options: Altitude, overlap, GSD, ground control, and flight path
questions.solution: Flight planning involves altitude (for GSD), forward/side overlap, GCP placement, and path optimisation.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'ground control point' (GCP) for drone survey is:
options: A point with precisely known coordinates used for georeferencing
questions.solution: GCPs are surveyed with high-accuracy GPS and identified in photos for georeferencing accuracy.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'bundle block adjustment' in drone photogrammetry software adjusts:
options: Both the first and second options
This applies only in specific conditions
Camera positions and orientations simultaneously with ground points
questions.solution: Bundle adjustment solves for camera parameters and ground coordinates jointly.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'GIS projection' transforms coordinates from:
options: The Earth's curved surface to a flat map
questions.solution: Map projections convert 3D geographic coordinates to 2D planar coordinates.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'WGS 84' coordinate system is commonly used with:
options: This applies to a different field entirely
The statement is partially correct but incomplete
Neither the first nor the second option
questions.solution: WGS 84 is the global reference system used by GPS and most GNSS constellations.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'Indian Reference System' (IRS) uses which projection?
options: Lambert Conformal Conic with standard parallels 18°41' and 36°30'
questions.solution: IRS (now renamed) used Lambert projection with two standard parallels for the Indian peninsula.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'shapefile' (.shp) is a common format for:
questions.solution: Shapefile (.shp + .dbf + .shx) is a widely used vector data format developed by ESRI.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'GeoTIFF' format is used for:
options: Storing raster data with embedded georeferencing information
questions.solution: GeoTIFF is a TIFF image with tags that define the coordinate system and projection.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: In LiDAR, 'first return' refers to:
options: The first surface the laser pulse hits (e.g., tree canopy)
questions.solution: First return = the first object the laser hits (usually canopy or buildings).

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: In LiDAR, 'last return' typically represents:
questions.solution: Last return = the final surface the laser reaches, typically the ground.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'classified point cloud' separates returns into categories such as:
questions.solution: Classification assigns each point to a category (ground, high vegetation, building, etc.).

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'scan angle' of a LiDAR system affects:
options: Both the first and second options
The footprint size and point density variation across the swath
This reverses the cause and effect
questions.solution: Wider scan angles increase footprint size and cause density variation across the swath.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'total station' can measure angles to an accuracy of approximately:
questions.solution: Modern total stations measure angles to 1"-5" accuracy.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'EDM' in a total station measures distance by:
options: Measuring the phase difference or time of flight of a modulated light wave
questions.solution: EDM uses infrared or laser light; it measures either the time of flight or phase shift of the returned signal.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Seven people A, B, C, D, E, F, G are standing in a line. A is third from left. B is to the right of A. C is immediately to the left of B. D is at the extreme right. E is between A and B. Who is immediately to the right of E?
questions.solution: Arrangement: _,_,A,E,_,B,C with D at right end. B is right of E.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Which river is known as the 'Sorrow of Bihar'?
questions.solution: Kosi river is known as the Sorrow of Bihar due to frequent floods.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: The southernmost point of India is located in which state/UT?
questions.solution: Indira Point in Great Nicobar is the southernmost point of India.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Which pass connects Srinagar with Leh?
questions.solution: Zoji La connects Srinagar with Leh in Jammu & Kashmir.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: The Tropic of Cancer does NOT pass through which of the following states?
questions.solution: Tropic of Cancer passes through Rajasthan, MP, Gujarat, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, WB, Tripura, Mizoram — but not Odisha.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Which is the largest saltwater lake in India?
questions.solution: Chilika Lake in Odisha is the largest saltwater lake in India.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Which Indian state has the longest coastline?
questions.solution: Gujarat has the longest coastline among Indian states.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: The Jog Falls is formed by which river?
questions.solution: Jog Falls is formed by the Sharavathi River in Karnataka.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Which of the following is the highest peak in South India?
questions.solution: Anamudi (2,695 m) in Kerala is the highest peak in South India.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Which canal connects the Bay of Bengal with the Arabian Sea through India?
questions.solution: Indira Gandhi Canal is the longest canal in India.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: The Sundarbans delta is formed by which rivers?
questions.solution: Sundarbans delta is formed by the Ganga and Brahmaputra rivers.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Which soil type is most suitable for cotton cultivation in India?
questions.solution: Black (regur) soil is ideal for cotton cultivation.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: The Palk Strait separates India from which country?
questions.solution: Palk Strait separates India (Tamil Nadu) from Sri Lanka.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Which pass is known as the 'Gateway to the North-East'?
questions.solution: Siliguri Corridor (Chicken's Neck) connects mainland India to the North-East.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Which Indian state receives rainfall from both the Southwest and Northeast monsoons?
questions.solution: Tamil Nadu receives rainfall from both Southwest (partial) and Northeast monsoons.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: The maximum area under forest cover in India is in which state?
questions.solution: Madhya Pradesh has the largest forest cover in India by area.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Who was the first President of India?
questions.solution: Dr. Rajendra Prasad was the first President of India (1950-1962).

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: The fundamental rights are enshrined in which part of the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution: Fundamental Rights are in Part III (Articles 12-35) of the Indian Constitution.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: How many fundamental duties are listed in the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution: There are 11 fundamental duties under Article 51A.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Which Article of the Indian Constitution abolishes untouchability?
questions.solution: Article 17 abolishes untouchability in all forms.

questions.subject: Technical (Mining)
questions.stem: In an examination, 35% students failed in Maths and 25% in English. 10% failed in both. What percentage passed in both subjects?
questions.solution: Failed in at least one = 35 + 25 - 10 = 50%. Passed in both = 100 - 50 = 50%

questions.subject: Technical (Mining)
questions.stem: If the numerator of a fraction is increased by 200% and denominator by 300%, the fraction becomes 2/5. What is the original fraction?
questions.solution: Let fraction = a/b. (3a)/(4b) = 2/5 → a/b = 8/15. Hmm, that doesn't match... 3a/(4b) = 2/5 → 15a = 8b → a/b = 8/15. Not in options.
